name: esp32-wroom-32e
title: ESP32-WROOM-32E with EN delay, BOOT button, auto-program and a CH340C USB-UART
about: The ESP32-WROOM-32E (no regulator on the module) with what its datasheet and Espressif's DevKitC V4 put around it: 10 kΩ / 1 µF RC delay at EN, 22 µF and 100 nF at 3V3, a BOOT button from IO0 to ground, and the auto-program circuit – two NPN transistors driven by DTR# and RTS# of a CH340C USB-UART at 3.3 V, so that esptool resets the module into the bootloader and a terminal that asserts both lines does not hold it in reset. The ports take a 3.3 V rail of at least 0.5 A and the D+/D− of a USB receptacle (block usb-c-data).

ports.3v3: the 3.3 V rail, at least 0.5 A (module datasheet table 14) – the block has no regulator
ports.usb_dp: USB D+ (to the receptacle's joined D+ behind its ESD protection, block usb-c-data)
ports.usb_dn: USB D− (to the receptacle's joined D−)

components.label: {as}: ESP32-WROOM-32E
components.notes: GPIOs in nc until the project uses them; strapping pins IO12 (low at power-up), IO2, IO15, IO5 – LVL.boot checks what is connected.

components.label: {as}: USB-UART CH340C
components.notes: 3.3 V operation: V3 joined to VCC; no crystal (built-in clock); unused MODEM inputs and R232 may float (datasheet note under the pin table).

nets.name: en
nets.notes: Chip enable: R1/C1 delay it at power-up, Q1 pulls it low for a reset.

nets.name: io0
nets.notes: Strapping pin GPIO0: high (internal pull-up) = SPI boot, low at reset = download boot – by SW1 or Q2.

accept.LVL.undefined: Not floating: the ESP32's U0TXD has its weak pull-up during and after reset (ESP32 Series Datasheet v5.3, table IO_MUX, pin 41: 'oe=0, ie=1, wpu') and the ROM bootloader drives it as U0TXD from boot on (U0TXD printing, table 3-4); the C701341 entry does not hold this pull.

notes: EN: 10 kΩ / 1 µF – 'the recommended setting for the RC delay circuit is usually R = 10 kΩ and C = 1 µF' (ESP32-WROOM-32E datasheet v2.1, 9 Peripheral Schematics; tSTBL ≥ 50 µs, table 9); esptool's boot-mode-selection page: with the two-transistor circuit a capacitor of 1–10 µF from EN to ground 'is necessary for the reset circuitry to work reliably'. The DevKitC V4 has 100 nF there (edakit's REQ.value finding on that design).

3V3: 22 µF + 100 nF at the module – C1/C2 of the module datasheet's figure 9 and C21/C22 of the DevKitC V4 (22 µF/10 V, 0.1 µF/50 V); the ESP32 Hardware Design Guidelines ask for at least a 10 µF on the rail for the Wi-Fi TX bursts (379 mA peak, module datasheet table 16), which 22 µF covers with room for the DC-bias loss of an 0805 X5R at 3.3 V.

BOOT: SW1 from IO0 to ground, no external pull-up and no capacitor – IO0's internal pull-up (about 45 kΩ) holds SPI boot (module datasheet table 4), the button is the strong pull-down esptool asks for; the DevKitC revision of 2018-06-07 marks the 100 nF across the BOOT button (C15) as not fitted.

Auto-program as on the DevKitC V4: Q1 base through 10 kΩ from DTR#, emitter on RTS#, collector on EN; Q2 base through 10 kΩ from RTS#, emitter on DTR#, collector on IO0. DTR#/RTS# pin levels → EN/IO0: 1/1 → 1/1, 0/0 → 1/1, 1/0 → 0/1 (reset), 0/1 → 1/0 (IO0 low while EN rises = download). S8050 (C2146, library) for the DevKitC's SS8050: a design choice – about 0.26 mA base current, hFE ≥ 200, VEB reverse at most 3.3 V against 5 V allowed.

CH340C at 3.3 V: VCC and V3 joined on 3v3 with 100 nF (CH340 datasheet 3C, pin table and 5.1); no crystal; UD+/UD− go straight to the USB lines – the transceiver and the USB pull-up are inside, no series resistors. One supply for CH340C and module (datasheet 7.6) – no current flows back through the I/O pins.

The module needs a 3.3 V supply of at least 0.5 A (datasheet table 14): an LDO block on 5 V (BL-5) or the board's own; a Pico's 3V3(OUT) (300 mA) is not enough – this is why the block's simulation fails in edakit's example (test table).

sim.json: the module's TXD0 net under its mcu outputs ({"mcu": {"U…": {"outputs": ["…_TXD"]}}}), so that the CH340C's RXD is simulated; the CH340C has no behaviour model (no supply current in the simulation).
The txd net carries an accept for LVL.undefined: the module entry lacks U0TXD's internal pull-up – remove the accept once the entry has "pull": "up" on TXD0.
A reset button is not part of the block: one from EN to ground if wanted (the module datasheet's figure 9 has it) – R1/C1 stay the EN delay, the button block's own 10 kΩ would double R1.
Before USB enumeration the CH340C reads DTR# as a configuration input (CH340 datasheet 5.1) – the state of Q1/Q2 in that moment is not checked by this block.
Keep copper away from the antenna end (the entry's antenna keep-out, GEO.keepout).

test.about: SIG and SIG2 stand in for the D+/D− of a USB receptacle, which the example lacks; the example's 3V3 comes from the Pico 2.
test.why: the example's 3V3 is the Pico 2's 3V3(OUT) (i_out_max_a 0.3 A); the ESP32-WROOM-32E alone draws up to 0.379 A (i_core_a, Wi-Fi TX peak) – LIM.i fails on U1 in every scenario (393 mA). With the module's TXD0 net as an mcu output the simulation has no other failure.
